diagnostics.message: module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_key_id: explicit depends_on of module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_access_key.this_user is redundant — already implied by attribute references
module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_secret_key: explicit depends_on of module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_access_key.this_user is redundant — already implied by attribute references

Output `access_key_id` sets `depends_on = [aws_iam_access_key.this_user]`, but its value (`aws_iam_access_key.this_user.id`) already references that same resource, so Terraform infers the dependency and the explicit depends_on is redundant.

Output `access_secret_key` sets `depends_on = [aws_iam_access_key.this_user]`, but its value (`aws_iam_access_key.this_user.secret`) already references that same resource, so the explicit depends_on is redundant.

`helm_release.elk` mounts the Secret `elastic-certificates` (secretMounts in elasticsearch/kibana/filebeat/apm/metricbeat) by literal name, but does not depend on the `kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates` that creates it. Pods will fail to start if the Secret is absent, so the release must be ordered after the Secret.

`helm_release.elk` reads the Secret `elastic-credentials` (secretKeyRef for ELASTICSEARCH_USERNAME/PASSWORD) by literal name but does not depend on `kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials`, so the chart may install before the Secret exists.

`helm_release.elk` references the keystore Secret `elasticsearch-s3-user-creds` by literal name but does not depend on `kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_s3_user_creds`, so the Secret may not exist when the chart is applied.

`helm_release.elk` references the kibana encryption-key Secret `kibana-encryption-key` by literal name but does not depend on `kubernetes_secret.kibana_enc_key`, so Kibana pods may fail to start if the Secret is absent.

`helm_release.elk` requests PVCs with `storageClassName: advanced` (literal string) but does not depend on `kubernetes_storage_class.advanced`; without ordering the volume claims can be created while the StorageClass is still missing and stay Pending.

`helm_release.loki_stack` sets `storageClassName: advanced` (literal string) for its PVC but does not depend on `kubernetes_storage_class.advanced`, so its volume claim may be created before the StorageClass exists.

`helm_release.prometheus_operator` sets `storageClassName: advanced` (literal string) in its prometheus volumeClaimTemplate but does not depend on `kubernetes_storage_class.advanced`, so the claim may be created before the StorageClass exists.

`helm_release.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack` sets `storageClassName: advanced` (literal string) in its vmsingle/alertmanager PVCs but does not depend on `kubernetes_storage_class.advanced`, so the claims may be created before the StorageClass exists.
